The A'i, better known as the Cofán, are an Indigenous people of the Amazon foothills on the border of Ecuador and Colombia, along the Aguarico and San Miguel rivers. Their language is an isolate. Jesuit missionaries worked among them in the 1600s, and epidemics cut their numbers to a few hundred.

In 1967 Texaco struck oil at Lago Agrio, in the heart of their land. Roads, settlers and oil pollution followed, and the Cofán joined the long lawsuit against the company over the damage. Since then they have won title to several reserves and run their own forest guard programmes. Their neighbours include the Secoya and Siona.
